chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Jamilah, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) say:

Six [groups] do not deserve to be greeted, and six do not deserve to lead the prayer, and six [acts] in this Ummah are from the character of the people of Lot. As for those who do not deserve to be greeted: the Jews, the Christians, the players of Nard and Backgammon, the drinkers of wine, the [players of] Barbat and Tanbur, those who joke by swearing at mothers, and the poets. And as for those who do not deserve to lead the prayer from among people: the child of fornication, the apostate, the Bedouin after migration, the drinker of wine and the one punished for it, and the uncircumcised. And as for that which is from the character of the people of Lot: Jalahiq (shooting round bullets with a sling), chewing gum, letting down the garment in pride, and unbuttoning the buttons of the cloak and shirt.

key_terms.الْأَعْرَابِيُّ بَعْدَ الْهِجْرَةِ: The Bedouin after migration (settling in cities)
key_terms.الْجَلَاهِق: Shooting round bullets with a sling

ai.seo_question: Who are the six groups that do not deserve to be greeted or lead prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) categorizes specific social and spiritual markers of distinction within the early Muslim community, linking ritual etiquette (greeting and leading prayer) to moral character. The classification reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *akhlaq* (morals) as indicators of religious standing, distinguishing between those excluded from communal leadership due to major sins or status, and those exhibiting the distinctive physical habits of the 'people of Lot' as a sign of moral decay.
